BOOK REVIEW:
WEED OUT BY TOSHAN NIMAI DAS

This is a short book about two people who unintentionally get caught up in the world of drugs and how they chose to deal with it.

Plot of the book:
Ankit and Tanmay are best friends who met in college and unfortunately get hooked on doing drugs for their own personal reasons.
Ankit, who comes from a wealthy background, attends these parties that are important for one to maintain a social status in the society and
became vulnerable to drinking during these events. Since his parents are working all the time and with his sister being away to attend
college, he becomes lonely and turns to drugs as his coping mechanism. This led to a downward spiral of his life as he started using drugs
on a daily basis and soon became a drug addict.
Tanmay,who is a junior to Ankit, comes from a background not as well as Ankit's. He started smoking, drinking alcohol and doing drugs
under the pressure of wanting to fit in among the other upper class men.
One day they both decide to want to leave this addiction by not going to rehab but also by finding out the drug cartels present in India
that are making the youth of this nation hardcore drug addicts.
Soon, Tanmay gets the news of Ankit's sudden death. This causes him to become depressed and disturbed and turned to alcohol as a coping mechanism.
After being persuaded by Ankit's sister Aarya, Tanmay finally joins a rehabilitation center to get over his addiction.
In there, he learns things which alters his way of living and perceiving things in life.
During this time, Aarya throws herself in finding more information about these drug suppliers, and she and Tanmay do not believe that
Ankit would ever take his own life.
Over the time,they both start discovering more information about the drug suppliers which could lead them in some serious trouble.
Did Ankit really kill himself? If not, who killed him? Read to find out.

Personal view:
The first thing that stands to me about this book is its unique title. Seeing this title, it makes me curious about what is the book about.
This book talks about how difficult it is to leave addiction of any kind but that does not mean it is impossible to do so.
It deals with the people who become addicted to drugs and wish to get over this addiction.
This book is unique in a way that it talks about social awareness and about youth that is thinly veiled in a murder mystery. It talks about how it is completely
normal to seek help in any way when we need it no matter how conflicting the society obligations may tell us so.
This book makes the readers think about certain aspects and it is as easy to follow as it is fun to read. The story has a gradual pace and
contains a healthy amount of suspense.
